key_insight: Visual-Attribution Gating (VAG) filters privileged teacher corrections to retain updates supported by visual evidence rather than non-visual influences.
engineering_relevance: VAG offers a way to combine verifiable task rewards with visually grounded token-level feedback when training multimodal reasoning models.
method: Anchor optimization with verifier-derived advantages from reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards.
Contrast evidence-present and evidence-degraded teacher views to assess visual support for each correction.
Admit directionally supported corrections and suppress inconsistent residuals during on-policy self-distillation.
evidence_signal: Across six visual reasoning benchmarks, the abstract reports consistent gains over GRPO and OPSD methods and a new state-of-the-art average performance, without numerical results.
watch_item: Gating reliability may depend on how evidence-degraded views are constructed; the abstract does not specify this procedure or its computational overhead.
paper_title: Reinforcement Learning with Visually Attributable On-Policy Self-Distillation
